questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a backing maneuver you will perform on the basic control skills test?
questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test includes: straight line backing, offset back/right, offset back/left, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: Leaf spring leaves:
questions.explanation: When you inspect a vehicle's suspension, check for broken or missing leaves in the leaf springs. This is dangerous. If one-fourth or more of the leaves are missing, the vehicle must be taken out of service.

questions.question: Bridges usually:

options.text: Freeze only when the temperature drops well below 32 degrees Fahrenheit.
Freeze after other road surfaces freeze.

questions.explanation: Bridges usually freeze before other roads. Be extra careful when crossing bridges if the temperature is near freezing.

questions.question: When driving, hold the steering wheel:

options.text: With both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.
With both hands at the bottom of the wheel.
With both hands at the top of the wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: With both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands placed on opposite sides.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle, you should:

options.text: Leave the keys in the ignition.

questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when you leave your vehicle.

questions.question: In cold weather, check and fill an alcohol evaporator:
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator prevents ice from building up in an air brake system. In cold weather, check and refill it every day.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal, air pressure activates an electric switch and:

options.text: Turn on the low pressure warning light.
Turn off the low pressure warning light.

questions.explanation: In a vehicle with air brakes, pressing the brake pedal causes air pressure to move an electric switch that turns on the brake lights.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT part of an air brake system?
questions.explanation: Air brakes have three separate systems: the service brake system, the parking brake system, and the emergency brake system.

questions.question: Which of the following is most likely to cause hydroplaning?
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens on wet roads when tire pressure is low or tire tread is worn. It can occur at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water on the road.

questions.question: Eating while driving:

options.text: Is a good way to save time.
Is a good idea on long trips.

questions.explanation: To avoid distracted driving, do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving. Anything that takes your attention away from driving is a distraction.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with a dual brake system, a driver should:

options.text: Let the engine warm up so fuel reaches it.
Wait for air pressure to build in both brake systems.
Start driving right after the engine starts.
Pump the pedal about 20 times to build pressure, then drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for air pressure to build in both brake systems.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, let the compressor build pressure to at least 100 psi in both systems.

questions.question: Brakes can go out of adjustment when:

options.text: One side is used more than the other side.

questions.explanation: Hot brakes are more likely to go out of adjustment. Use proper braking techniques to prevent your brakes from overheating.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, you should:
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, create more space in front of your vehicle. This helps you avoid sudden stops and makes it easier for them to pass. Speeding up makes things more dangerous.

questions.question: During the pre-trip inspection test, you will:

options.text: Explain what you know about the pre-trip inspection process.
Watch someone else check your vehicle.
Watch a film about how to inspect a vehicle.
Change all the tires on your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain what you know about the pre-trip inspection process.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you will inspect your vehicle and explain what you are checking and why.

questions.question: A thin layer of ice on a road surface is called:
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it. A road with black ice looks wet. Be careful when it is below freezing and the road looks wet.

questions.question: When making tight turns, a driver should:

options.text: Open the door to see better.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly while driving. Check them especially when changing lanes, turning, merging, or making tight turns.

questions.question: Most heavy-duty vehicles use:
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles use dual air brake systems. These have two separate braking systems operated by one set of controls. Each system controls the brakes on different axles.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when:

options.text: Tires lose grip on the road surface.
Tires gain more grip on the road surface.
Front tires have more grip than rear tires.
Front tires have less grip than rear tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tires lose grip on the road surface.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs on wet roads when tires lose grip and slide on a layer of water.

questions.question: When doing a driver's side parallel parking maneuver, you should:

options.text: Pass the space while backing, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
Pull forward into the space without passing it first.
Back into the space without passing it first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space, then back into it. Bring the rear of your vehicle close to the rear of the space. Your vehicle must fit completely within the space.

questions.question: After a trailer starts to turn while backing, you should follow it by:

options.text: Doing nothing. The vehicle will follow naturally.
Turning the steering wheel in the opposite direction.
Turning the steering wheel further in the same direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning the steering wheel in the opposite direction.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, turn the steering wheel the opposite way of where you want to go. Once the trailer starts to turn, turn the steering wheel the other way to follow it.

questions.question: If you are not sure there is enough space for your vehicle to pass safely under a bridge, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve as you pass under the bridge.

questions.explanation: If you are not sure you have enough room to safely fit under a bridge or overhead object, slow down. Try to find an alternate route if possible.

questions.question: What do slippery roadways usually do?

options.text: Make it more difficult to stop a vehicle.
Make it easier to stop a vehicle.
Make it easier to drive a vehicle.
Can be avoided by driving at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make it more difficult to stop a vehicle.
questions.explanation: It takes longer to stop on a slippery road than on a dry road. Drive with caution when road conditions are wet or slippery.

questions.question: When operating a CMV (commercial motor vehicle), what is required regarding safety belts?

options.text: You are not required to wear a safety belt.
You are only required to wear a safety belt if your vehicle does not have airbags.
You are required to wear a safety belt only if hauling more than 1,000 pounds of cargo.
You are always required to wear a safety belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are always required to wear a safety belt.
questions.explanation: A safety belt protects you during a crash. You must always wear a safety belt when operating a CMV.

questions.question: How can you help your vehicle be seen by others?

options.text: Turn off your headlights during the day.
Use your headlights only in the rain.

questions.explanation: Clean headlights provide more light and help other drivers see your vehicle. Always keep your headlights clean when driving.

questions.question: While driving, what holds spring brakes in place?
questions.explanation: While driving, air pressure holds spring brakes in place. If air pressure drops too low, the springs will activate the brakes.

questions.question: When checking the engine compartment, what should you do?

options.text: The parking brake should not be engaged.
Put the gearshift in first gear.

questions.explanation: Before inspecting the engine, engage the parking brake and chock the wheels. Do this before you enter the cab and start the engine.

questions.question: What should you do if the air pressure warning light comes on while driving?

options.text: Turn on your hazard lights and keep driving.
Safely exit the roadway and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safely exit the roadway and stop.
questions.explanation: If the air pressure warning light or buzzer comes on, stop immediately and park safely. This warning means there is a problem with the air brake system that needs repair.

questions.question: What is the minimum size allowed for a hazmat placard?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be diamond-shaped and at least 10 ¾ square inches in size.

questions.question: What does the air compressor do in an air brake system on a truck?

options.text: Pumps air into the air storage tanks.
Moves air to the back of the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pumps air into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks. The air compressor governor controls the air compressor.

questions.question: What is aggressive driving?

options.text: Operating a vehicle in a selfish or pushy manner without regard for others' safety
Operating a vehicle with some regard for other motorists' safety
Operating a vehicle in the left lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Operating a vehicle in a selfish or pushy manner without regard for others' safety
questions.explanation: Aggressive driving means operating a vehicle in a selfish or pushy manner without regard for the rights or safety of others.

questions.question: Loose belts in an engine compartment will:

options.text: Prevent the water pump and/or fan from working properly, causing the engine to overheat.
Make the engine run more efficiently.
Make the fan work too hard, causing the engine to run too cold.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent the water pump and/or fan from working properly, causing the engine to overheat.
questions.explanation: Check that belts in your engine are tight. Loose belts will not turn the water pump and/or fan correctly. This can cause the engine to overheat.

questions.question: For an offset back/right parking maneuver, you should:

options.text: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
Pull forward to the right, then back in a straight line.
Pull forward to the left, then back in a straight line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
questions.explanation: To do an offset back/right parking maneuver, pull straight forward first. Then back up to the right. Your vehicle must fit completely within the parking space lines.

questions.question: If your truck or trailer catches fire, you should:

options.text: Park in a busy area near trees.

questions.explanation: If your vehicle catches fire, leave the road and stop right away. Park in an open area away from trees and other vehicles that could catch fire. Do not go to a gas station.

questions.question: When driving in heavy traffic, you should:

options.text: Text instead of call on your cell phone.
Turn up the volume on your cell phone ringer.

questions.explanation: Heavy traffic, road construction, crowds of pedestrians, and bad weather require your full attention. Avoid all distractions, including using your cell phone.

questions.question: How do you release the parking brake?

options.text: By tapping the brake pedal three times
By pushing in the brake control knob

questions.correctAnswerText: By pushing in the brake control knob
questions.explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, the parking brake is controlled with a yellow diamond-shaped knob. Pull the knob out to apply the parking brake. Push it in to release it.

questions.question: The drive shaft should:

options.text: Be bent toward the passenger side.
Be bent toward the driver's side.
Be bent to one side or the other.

questions.explanation: During a vehicle safety inspection, check that the drive shaft is not bent or cracked.

questions.question: If federal inspectors find your vehicle unsafe, they can:

options.text: Take you to a garage to fix your vehicle.
Formally ask you to have your vehicle's problems fixed.
Pull your vehicle out of service until it is fixed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull your vehicle out of service until it is fixed.
questions.explanation: Federal or state inspectors can take a vehicle out of service if they decide it is unsafe. The vehicle must stay out of service until all problems are fixed.

questions.question: When entering a curve, you should:
questions.explanation: Always take turns and curves at a safe speed. Downshift before you enter a curve.

questions.question: Cargo on a flatbed trailer or trailer without sides must be:

options.text: Loose so it can shift when the vehicle turns.
Heavy enough that it won't shift.

questions.explanation: Cargo on a flatbed trailer or open trailer must be securely tied down. This keeps it from moving or falling off while driving.

questions.question: When carrying a sealed load, the driver should:

options.text: Make sure the cargo weight does not exceed weight limits.
Open each container to check it.
Unseal the load to check for safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the cargo weight does not exceed weight limits.
questions.explanation: You cannot inspect sealed loads, but you must check that the cargo weight does not exceed the allowed gross weight and axle weight limits.

questions.question: When using your mirrors, you should frequently look at your tires to:

options.text: See if the tires are rolling properly.
Check if the tread is worn enough.
Compare the tire size to other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Check your tires regularly in your mirrors. This helps you notice a tire fire if one starts. Tire fires happen when a tire is not fully inflated, when dual tires touch each other, or when tires overheat.

questions.question: When checking the springs during a vehicle inspection, do all of the following except:

options.text: Make sure torsion springs are not damaged.

questions.explanation: When inspecting springs, look for missing, shifted, cracked, or broken leaf springs. Also check for broken or bent coil springs. If your vehicle has torsion bars or other suspension parts, make sure they are not damaged and are securely mounted.

questions.question: During a static leakage test, the maximum air leak for a single vehicle with air brakes is ____ in one minute.
questions.explanation: In a static leakage test on a single vehicle with air brakes, air should leak no more than 2 psi in one minute. If air leaks faster, do not drive the vehicle. Something needs repair.

questions.question: When traveling with cargo, you must check that it is secure:

options.text: Every 150 miles or every three hours of driving.
Only after traveling up a hill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every 150 miles or every three hours of driving.
questions.explanation: Check cargo before you start, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles. The driver is responsible for keeping cargo safely secured the entire trip.

questions.question: When covering cargo, a cover that flaps while driving:

options.text: Lets air reach the cargo to keep it cool.

questions.explanation: Cargo covers should not flap in the wind while driving. A flapping cover can tear loose and uncover your cargo. It may also block your view or others' views of the road.

questions.question: After changing a tire, you should stop after a short distance to:

options.text: Make sure the lug nuts are tight.
Check how much the tire has worn.
Check the windshield wiper fluid level.
Check the air pressure of the new tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After you change a tire, stop after a short distance to check that the lug nuts are still tight and secure.

questions.question: To use the stab braking method, you should:

options.text: Press the brakes fully until the wheels lock, release until the wheels roll again, then repeat.
Press the brakes about halfway while keeping the wheels rolling.
Press the brakes fully until the wheels lock and the vehicle stops.
Press the emergency brake until the vehicle starts to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brakes fully until the wheels lock, release until the wheels roll again, then repeat.
questions.explanation: In stab braking for an emergency stop, press the brakes all the way until they lock. Then release the brakes until the wheels start rolling again. Repeat this process.

questions.question: When driving with a load, the driver should:

options.text: Stop and check the cargo within the first 50 miles of the trip.
Ask other drivers about their cargo condition.
Use only the side mirrors to check the cargo.
Not check the cargo if it was properly secured before starting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and check the cargo within the first 50 miles of the trip.
questions.explanation: Inspect cargo and how it is secured before you start. After starting, check the cargo and securing devices within the first 50 miles, every three hours or 150 miles, and after every break.

questions.question: During the straight line backing exercise, how many times can you exit the vehicle to check its position?
questions.explanation: During the straight line backing exercise, you may exit your vehicle to check its position only one time.

questions.question: After starting a trip while transporting cargo:

options.text: You do not need to inspect the cargo.
Inspect the cargo only if it is making noise.
Inspect the cargo only if there is an obvious problem.
Inspect the cargo after 50 miles to make sure it is still properly secured.

questions.correctAnswerText: Inspect the cargo after 50 miles to make sure it is still properly secured.
questions.explanation: Check that cargo is secure before starting, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles.
